sentences.text: NOTE 02. 02.12.2025 BVLNC,J I.A.No.01 of 2024 Heard Sri T.Nageswara Rao, learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant and Sri A.Sai Rohith, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor representing the State.

Learned counsel for the  petitioner/convict would submit that the appellant was found guilty for the offence under Sections 417, 376(2)(n) of I.P.C., Sections 4, 5(1)
r/w 6 of POCSO Act, 2012 and he was sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of twenty (20) years and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand only), in default, to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of one (01) month for the offence under Section 5(1) r/w Section 6 of POCSO Act, 2012 and further sentenced to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of six (06)
months and to pay a fine of Rs.500/- (Rupees Five Hundred only), in default, to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of one (01) month for the offence U/s.417 IPC.
Both the sentences shall run concurrently.
The petitioner/appellant filed application to suspend the sentence, pending disposal of the appeal.

Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor opposed the application contending that during the trial, bail of the appellant was cancelled, as he was violated the conditions and the alleged offence is a grave offence, and he was sentenced to suffer imprisonment for a period of twenty (20) years and opposed the application.
Undisputedly, the appellant/convict was sentenced to suffer imprisonment for a period of twenty (20) years for the offence under Section 5(1) r/w Section 6 of POCSO Act.

Before parting with the matter, this Court would like to note that the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Lilaben Vs. State of Gujarat and Others1, which is a case under POCSO Act 2012, observed that "sentence imposed for 20 years is greater than life imprisonment".
Considering the facts of the case, gravity of offence, the manner in which it was committed, this Court is of the considered opinion that it is not a fit case to suspend the order of sentence.
